record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Develop an input-to-output stability theory for infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, analogous to the mature finite-dimensional IOS theory. This includes general criteria, Lyapunov tools, and structural results for systems where the quantity of interest is an output h(x,u) rather than the full state.

evidence.quote: For finite-dimensional systems the IOS theory is quite rich, see, e.g., [4, 212, 222]. There is almost no result on IOS theory in the context of infinite-dimensional systems (except for delay systems). Some exceptions include the small-gain results for IOS systems in [12, 111].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$ where $X$ is a Banach space (the state space), $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$ (with $U$ a normed input-value space), and $\phi:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times X\times\mathcal{U}\to X$ is a transition map satisfying the standard axioms of a forward-complete control system (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity in initial state). Equip the system with an output map $h:X\times U\to Y$ taking values in a Banach output space $Y$; write $H(t,x,u):=h(\phi(t,x,u),u(t))$.

Recall the standard comparison-function classes: $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{KL}$. The system $(\Sigma,h)$ is called input-to-output stable (IOS) if there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x\in X$, every $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and every $t\geq 0$,
$$\|H(t,x,u)\|_Y \;\leq\; \beta(\|x\|_X,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}).$$

Develop a theory of input-to-output stability for such infinite-dimensional systems with outputs that parallels the finite-dimensional IOS theory. In particular, address the following:

1. (Superposition / characterization theorem.) Identify weaker stability-like properties (analogues of output asymptotic gain, output Lagrange stability, output limit property, output continuity at the equilibrium, etc.) whose conjunction is equivalent to IOS, and determine which combinations are sufficient versus insufficient in the infinite-dimensional setting.

2. (Lyapunov characterizations.) Define an appropriate notion of IOS Lyapunov function $V:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ involving the output norm $\|h(x,u)\|_Y$, and prove that the existence of such a function is equivalent (or, where this fails, obtain the strongest possible implications) to IOS.

3. (Structural / small-gain results.) Establish small-gain theorems for feedback interconnections and (possibly infinite) networks of IOS subsystems on Banach spaces, giving verifiable conditions on the gain operators that guarantee IOS of the interconnection.

Provide the criteria, Lyapunov tools, and structural results, and identify intrinsic obstructions specific to the infinite-dimensional case (e.g., examples showing classical finite-dimensional equivalences fail).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2024 preprint titled "Characterization of input-to-output stability for infinite-dimensional systems", arXiv:2410.06013) provides superposition-type characterizations of IOS for broad classes of infinite-dimensional continuous- and discrete-time systems with outputs, in terms of weaker properties (OUAG, OULS, OCEP, etc.), and shows that some finite-dimensional characterizations cannot be extended verbatim. Small-gain results for IOS networks of infinite-dimensional systems have also appeared. However, a full theory paralleling the finite-dimensional case—including complete Lyapunov characterizations and a comprehensive structural framework—is still under development, so the program is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of input-to-output stability for infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: We prove a superposition theorem for input-to-output stability (IOS) of a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs... characterized in terms of weaker properties such as OUAG, OULS, OCEP.
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterizations of IOS in the infinite-dimensional setting have recently been obtained.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems: recent results and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: There is almost no result on IOS theory in the context of infinite-dimensional systems (except for delay systems).
status_evidence.claim: As of the survey, IOS theory for infinite-dimensional systems was largely undeveloped.
